body: Would it make sense to also push the code of the release on a GitHub tag? This will allow us to track what's been released.
diff_hunk:
@@ -217,3 +216,21 @@ npm run release -- --beta
 ```
 
 _Make sure to use `npm run` instead of `yarn run` to avoid issues._
+
+#### Experimental TypeScript version
+
+An experimental version containing the TypeScript declaration files is available.
+
+Since some of these declaration files are generated from the JSDoc comments they can still contains some typing errors. This version will stay experimental until we are confident enough in the generated declarations to put them in the stable release.
+
+To generate the experimental TypeScript version for a particular release run:
+
+```sh
+git checkout v4.X.X
+VERSION=4.X.X-experimental-typescript.X node ./scripts/release/bump-package-version.js
+yarn build
+yarn build:types
+sed -i '/"main":/ a \ "types": "es/index.d.ts",' package.json # Add `types` entry in `package.json`
+npm publish --tag experimental-typescript
+git checkout .
+```

body:
We need this change because in semver `4.X.X-experimental-typescript.X` < `4.X.X` and `semver.gte` will then return false. This is a problem if we want to do the TypeScript release after the stable one (what we'll most likely do).

This change allows us to publish prereleases of the `currentVersion`.
I don't think so. Since we will not push the changes for `experimental-typescript` to GitHub, the tag would always be on the same commit as for the stable one (ex: on `v4.X.X` in the script above).

body: I see – I think that'd be worth adding a comment explaining why this line is here then.

Are you reluctant to this because it's more work to do on our side or because it doesn't provide value?

Ideally, you should be able to map an npm release with a GitHub tag. If we release without publishing the source code related to this release, it's like we "blindly" release without having the ability to check (even later), what this release contained.

I see this as an improvement (that could be handled by Ship.js later), not as a blocker.
